newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns Bangkok Bank individual rating of B/C.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns Bangkok Bank individual rating of B/C.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had assigned Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, an individual rating of B/C and a legal rating of 2.

IBCA said in a statement that its rating reflected the prospective deterioration in Thailand's economic environment, which could be expected to some degree to impact negatively Bangkok Bank's balance sheet.
"The bank's good performance record would warrant a higher ranking, were it not for the uncertainty created by Thailand's impending economic slowdown," the statement said.

IBCA said the individual rating was an evaluation of the bank's financial strength based on the premise that it was entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners.

The highest Individual rating awarded by IBCA is A. Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if it ran into trouble. IBCA said Bangkok Bank had developed a strong franchise throughout the South-East Asian region and maintained in excess of 20 percent loan and deposit market shares in its home market.

In common with other Thai banks, Bangkok Bank had benefited from a favourable operating environment in recent years, experiencing buoyant growth in revenues and loan assets and a low level of loan losses.

Non performing loans accounted for less than four percent of loans at March 1996. Notwithstanding its dominant market position, Bangkok Bank's performance ratios were not as impressive as some of its rivals, in part because the bank provided more than it needs to in good years in order to smooth its profitability in subsequent years.

"Therefore, the level of provisioning does not truly reflect the quality of the loan book but should ensure that profitability is not severely affected by the expected slowdown in the Thai economy," the statement added.
